## Overview

**Core question:** Do uniform-buffer declarations, descriptors, and shader loads agree with the layout selected for each generated `ubo` case?

- This page covers the `ubo` test category registered by [`ubo::createTests()`](../../../modules/vulkan/ubo/vktUniformBlockTests.cpp#L1260-L1263) and implemented by [`UniformBlockTests::init()`](../../../modules/vulkan/ubo/vktUniformBlockTests.cpp#L446-L1256).
- The 15 direct test families combine fixed block shapes with deterministic random interfaces. They vary layout qualifiers, member types, arrays, structs, block instances, buffer placement, shader stages, and selected feature paths.
- Shared infrastructure calculates a host reference layout, writes deterministic values, generates each case's GLSL, runs a graphics or compute pipeline, and requires an all-white result image.
- The page explains the registered families, their behavioral differences, generated shader strategy, runtime flow, feature pruning, and the meaning of a non-white result.

## Background Knowledge

- A `VK_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE_UNIFORM_BUFFER` descriptor associates a buffer resource with a shader structure whose members can be loaded. A descriptor-set layout defines each binding's descriptor type, count, and stages that can access it.
- Vulkan defines scalar, base, and extended alignment for members of explicitly laid-out structures. Matrices behave as arrays of vectors. With `scalarBlockLayout`, `Uniform` members use scalar alignment; a `Uniform` block otherwise uses extended alignment unless `uniformBufferStandardLayout` permits base alignment.
- `minUniformBufferOffsetAlignment` constrains the offset in `VkDescriptorBufferInfo`. It matters when several tested blocks use ranges within one buffer.

## Registration Hierarchy

```text
ubo
├── 2_level_array
├── 2_level_struct_array
├── 3_level_array
├── instance_array_basic_type
├── link_by_binding
├── multi_basic_types
├── multi_nested_struct
├── random
├── single_basic_array
├── single_basic_type
├── single_nested_struct
├── single_nested_struct_array
├── single_struct
├── single_struct_array
└── unsized_array
```

[`TestPackage::init()`](../../../modules/vulkan/vktTestPackage.cpp#L1345-L1356) registers `ubo` for Vulkan, and [`TestPackageSC::init()`](../../../modules/vulkan/vktTestPackage.cpp#L1413-L1424) does the same for Vulkan SC. The direct families above match the roots represented in `vk-default/ubo.txt` and `vksc-default/ubo.txt`; deeper paths are generated by the registration loops.

## Behavior Parameters

The primary behavioral axis is the direct `ubo` test family. Each family changes the declaration shape or interface relationship that the common reference-layout and comparison machinery exercises.

### 2_level_array — nested basic-type arrays

This family checks two-level arrays whose inner and outer sizes are `4` and `3`. It applies each registered layout and adds matrix-major variants when the element type is a matrix.

### 2_level_struct_array — nested arrays of structs

This family places nested struct arrays in a block and runs per-block and single-buffer arrangements. The single-buffer case only appears with an instance array because a shared buffer needs more than one block instance to distinguish its placement behavior.

### 3_level_array — three-level basic-type arrays

This family adds a third array level with sizes `2`, `4`, and `3`. It uses the same layout and matrix-major dimensions as the two-level array family, but exposes another level of recursive stride calculation.

### instance_array_basic_type — basic members in block-instance arrays

This family declares arrays of three block instances for each basic type and layout. The generated comparisons select every instance that belongs to the declared shader stage.

### link_by_binding — same block name across graphics stages

This family constructs two `TestBlock` declarations with the same block name, one for the vertex stage and one for the fragment stage. Its four leaves vary `single_buf` or `per_block_buf` placement and single-instance or two-instance arrays.

### multi_basic_types — multiple blocks with basic members

This family creates `BlockA` and `BlockB` with different scalar, vector, matrix, and boolean members. Its `mixed` variants declare `BlockA` for the vertex shader and `BlockB` for the fragment shader.

### multi_nested_struct — multiple blocks with nested structs

This family extends the multiple-block arrangement with structs `S` and `T`, arrays, matrices, and unused members. It uses the same buffer-placement, instance-array, stage, and matrix-load dimensions as `multi_basic_types`.

### random — deterministic generated interfaces

This family builds numbered cases from a registered base seed plus the command-line base seed. Its normal, `16bit`, and `8bit` intermediate nodes select groups such as `scalar_types`, `nested_structs_arrays`, `all_per_block_buffers`, `all_shared_buffer`, `all_out_of_order_offsets`, `scalar`, and `descriptor_indexing`.

### single_basic_array — one array member

This family creates an array of size `3` for each basic type and layout. Matrix cases also select `row_major` or `column_major` declarations and component-access leaves.

### single_basic_type — one basic member

This family isolates one basic block member. It registers `lowp`, `mediump`, and `highp` groups only for types that support precision modifiers, then creates stage and matrix-load leaves.

### single_nested_struct — one nested struct member

This family places nested structs `S` and `T` with matrix, vector, and scalar members in one block. It combines layouts, buffer placement, optional block-instance arrays, stages, and matrix component access.

### single_nested_struct_array — nested structs with arrays

This family adds struct arrays inside the nested structure. Its dimensions match `single_nested_struct`, while the declaration shape adds array strides to the reference layout.

### single_struct — one struct member

This family puts struct `S` in one block. `S` contains an unused integer vector, an array of four `mat3` values, and a vector, so the generated comparisons skip the explicitly unused member and check the remaining members.

### single_struct_array — an array of structs with surrounding members

This family places `u`, an array of three `S` structs, and `v` in one block. The surrounding members make offsets before and after the struct array observable.

### unsized_array — final unsized block member

This family places an unsized array as the block's last member and assigns a test size of `19`. It creates vertex, fragment, compute, and combined graphics leaves, plus matrix component-access leaves for matrix types.

## Shader Analysis

The test generates GLSL from each selected interface rather than storing a fixed shader. [`UniformBlockCase::delayedInit()`](../../../modules/vulkan/ubo/vktUniformBlockCase.cpp#L2623-L2669) computes the reference layout, fills values, and selects [`generateVertexShader()`](../../../modules/vulkan/ubo/vktUniformBlockCase.cpp#L1755-L1803), [`generateFragmentShader()`](../../../modules/vulkan/ubo/vktUniformBlockCase.cpp#L1805-L1853), or [`generateComputeShader()`](../../../modules/vulkan/ubo/vktUniformBlockCase.cpp#L1855-L1911).

The declaration generator emits `layout(set = 0, binding = ...) uniform` blocks from the selected block layout, members, instance names, and arrays. The comparison generator recursively visits basic values, arrays, and struct members, skips members marked unused for the active graphics stage, and compares each applicable load against host-generated reference values. Compute shaders write their final comparison value to a storage image; graphics shaders propagate vertex and fragment comparison results through color channels.

No representative shader or SPIR-V listing appears here. A faithful listing requires one exact registered case and its generator branches; this page documents the generator behavior and does not hand-author generated shader or SPIR-V material.

## Runtime Execution and Result Checking

- [`UniformBlockCase::delayedInit()`](../../../modules/vulkan/ubo/vktUniformBlockCase.cpp#L2623-L2669) computes the reference layout, allocates reference bytes, fills them with `generateValues(..., 1)`, and generates the selected shader sources.
- [`UniformBlockCaseInstance::createDescriptorSetLayout()`](../../../modules/vulkan/ubo/vktUniformBlockCase.cpp#L2458-L2524) creates `VK_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE_UNIFORM_BUFFER` bindings. Compute cases add one `VK_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE_STORAGE_IMAGE` binding after the maximum UBO binding.
- The runtime uploads each block to a separate buffer in `per_block_buffer` mode. In `single_buffer` mode, it copies blocks into one buffer at offsets aligned to `minUniformBufferOffsetAlignment`, then creates descriptors for those ranges.
- Graphics cases draw an indexed full-screen quad into an `R8G8B8A8_UNORM` color image. Compute cases dispatch `RENDER_WIDTH` by `RENDER_HEIGHT` workgroups with a `1x1x1` local size and store results in the image.
- The runtime copies the image to a host-visible result buffer, counts pixels that differ from white, and reports failure if any such pixel exists.

## Failure Meaning

### Failure Cause Mapping

| If this behavior parameter value fails | Possible failure cause(s) |
|----------------------------------------|---------------------------|
| `2_level_array` | Nested-array layout, stride, or generated array-load comparison failure. |
| `2_level_struct_array` | Nested struct-array layout, buffer placement, or generated member-load comparison failure. |
| `3_level_array` | Three-level array layout, stride, or generated array-load comparison failure. |
| `instance_array_basic_type` | Uniform-block instance-array descriptor indexing, layout, or generated load failure. |
| `link_by_binding` | Descriptor binding linkage for same-named blocks across graphics stages or buffer-placement failure. |
| `multi_basic_types` | Multi-block descriptor placement, type-layout, stage-selection, or generated comparison failure. |
| `multi_nested_struct` | Multi-block nested-struct layout, descriptor placement, stage-selection, or generated comparison failure. |
| `random` | Deterministic generated interface layout, feature-specific declaration, descriptor indexing, or generated comparison failure. |
| `single_basic_array` | Array layout, stride, matrix-layout, or generated array-load comparison failure. |
| `single_basic_type` | Basic-member layout, stage-selection, or generated comparison failure. |
| `single_nested_struct` | Nested-struct layout, buffer placement, or generated member-load comparison failure. |
| `single_nested_struct_array` | Nested struct-array layout, buffer placement, or generated member-load comparison failure. |
| `single_struct` | Struct layout, buffer placement, or generated member-load comparison failure. |
| `single_struct_array` | Struct-array layout, buffer placement, or generated member-load comparison failure. |
| `unsized_array` | Uniform-buffer unsized-array layout, runtime size handling, or generated array-load comparison failure. |

### Cause Analysis

#### Uniform-block layout, stride, and member-load failures

**Possible failure symptoms:** The result image contains one or more non-white pixels. The log records the number of non-white pixels and the generated block and uniform layout entries.

**Possible implementation causes:** The selected case exposes a mismatch in handling the relevant `Uniform` member alignment, matrix stride, array stride, member offset, or generated load. Vulkan defines scalar, base, and extended alignment rules, including the matrix-as-array relationship; the test's source computes the reference layout before generating declarations and comparisons.

#### Descriptor placement, binding, and stage-selection failures

**Possible failure symptoms:** A non-white result indicates that at least one generated comparison for an applicable stage or block instance did not match the reference value. This includes `single_buffer`, block-instance-array, same-name block, and `mixed` cases.

**Possible implementation causes:** The case may expose a mismatch in the descriptor range offset, descriptor array element, binding association, stage visibility, or the host packing of blocks into a shared buffer. The runtime aligns shared-buffer offsets to `minUniformBufferOffsetAlignment`, and descriptor-set layout bindings record a descriptor type, count, and accessible stages.

#### Generated-interface or feature-specific failures

**Possible failure symptoms:** A supported `random`, 8-bit, 16-bit, `std430`, `scalar`, descriptor-indexing, or unsized-array case produces non-white pixels. Unsupported requirements produce `NotSupportedError` during the support check instead of this image-comparison failure.

**Possible implementation causes:** The source-level evidence shows feature gates and generated declarations for these paths. A non-white result can arise from handling the selected generated layout, type, descriptor array, or unsized-array interface differently from the generated reference. Determining whether the cause lies in compilation, descriptors, or execution requires the logged layout entries and source-level investigation for the exact failing path.

## Case Pruning

### Requirement-based pruning

[`UniformBlockCase::checkSupport()`](../../../modules/vulkan/ubo/vktUniformBlockCase.cpp#L2671-L2691) marks a case unsupported when its required capability is absent:

- 16-bit storage requires `uniformAndStorageBuffer16BitAccess`.
- 8-bit storage requires `uniformAndStorageBuffer8BitAccess`.
- `std430` requires `scalarBlockLayout` or `uniformBufferStandardLayout`; `scalar` requires `scalarBlockLayout`.
- Descriptor-indexing cases require `shaderUniformBufferArrayNonUniformIndexing` and `runtimeDescriptorArray`.
- Unsized-array cases require `shaderUniformBufferUnsizedArray` outside Vulkan SC builds.

### Design-based pruning

- The fixed `single_buffer` struct-family loops omit non-instance variants because the registration comments state that those variants do not make sense.
- The random generator limits block counts, members, struct depth, instances, and array length. It reduces an array to length `1` when its calculated complexity reaches `70` or more.
- The random descriptor-indexing generator tracks available uniform-buffer descriptors from the minimum `maxPerStageDescriptorUniformBuffers` value of `12` before adding generated block arrays.

## Key Takeaways

- The `ubo` test family compares device-side uniform loads with host-generated values placed according to a source-calculated reference layout.
- Fixed families isolate a declaration shape, while `random` combines deterministic generated interfaces with registered feature sets and seeds.
- A white image means every generated comparison passed. A non-white image identifies a mismatch but does not, by itself, assign the defect to shader compilation, descriptor handling, layout interpretation, or execution.
- `single_buffer` cases separately exercise the device limit on uniform-buffer descriptor offsets; block-layout rules do not replace that descriptor-range alignment requirement.
